text:
ana: FYI hitting a weird SSE resume issue seen in quickstart on browser + mobile webview. Sometimes after a network blip the client gets the previous token again even though we set Last-Event-ID on reconnect. Repro steps in /examples/stream-resume-web.
mike: can you share the raw bytes or a small capture? is this Node only or browser too?
ana: browser + webview + Node all hit it. Capture shows server sent two events with ids 2001 and 2002. The network trace shows the proxy coalesced the two writes so the browser read delivered both events in a single read, but with only one trailing CRLF. If the client aborts mid-read and reconnects with Last-Event-ID:2001 the server re-emits 2001. Our browser SDK then delivers 2001 again.
yun: interesting. Mobile webviews sometimes drop trailing blank lines when the native stack buffers. Also some service workers re-serialize bodies which can affect boundaries. Did you log the `id` field before emitting?
ana: we weren't; the quickstart used a naive split-on-"\n\n" parser and emitted whatever parsed. That means if the parser sees two events in one buffer but the boundary is malformed it can yield both, then on reconnect the server resends the last event id.

mike: two angles to fix for parity and DX: (1) SDK-level dedupe by `id` during the session and across reconnects (keep small LRU or ring buffer), (2) make the parser tolerant to single-line separators and optionally flush partial events after a short configurable timeout. Also expose the `id` to the user-level event so apps can dedupe too.

proxy-bot: note: some ingress configs (nginx/h2, cloud load balancers) will coalesce application writes. TLS and HTTP/2 frame boundaries are not event boundaries.

yun: implementation notes: dedupe policy should be conservative: keep last N ids (configurable, default 512) with a TTL (e.g., 5m) to avoid unbounded memory growth for very long streams. On reconnect, if an event id already seen, skip emitting it. Also emit a debug metric `sse.dedup_skipped` and a trace point so ops can spot server-side resends.

mike: parser approach: default strict mode keeps current behavior (wait for blank line). Add `sse.lenientNewlineFlushMs` default 0. If >0, when we detect a single LF between events schedule a flush after that many ms; if more bytes come before the timer fires, cancel and parse normally. This improves latency for coalesced frames without breaking strict semantics.

ana: small repro snippet (browser):
```js
const r = await fetch(url, {headers: {Accept: 'text/event-stream'}});
const reader = r.body.getReader();
while(true){
  const {done, value} = await reader.read();
  if(done) break;
  console.log(new TextDecoder().decode(value));
}
```
This shows two events in one read.

qa-bot: QA found nginx config that reproduces reliably: `proxy_buffering on` with small buffers, and an artificial server that writes `id: X\ndata: {...}\n` then `id: X+1\ndata: {...}\n` with no extra flush. Also repros on Chrome mobile webview.

mike: action items:
- mike: open SDK issues (web/node/go) for `sse.dedupeById` + `sse.lenientNewlineFlushMs` and include unit + integration tests
- yun: add an integration harness (docker-compose with nginx and a tiny streaming server) that intentionally splits/coalesces frames and runs E2Es for all SDKs
- ana: add quickstart example and docs explaining Last-Event-ID semantics and the `dedupe` flag as workaround before servers change flush behavior
- proxy-bot: scan hosted ingress configs for buffering defaults and flag any that could coalesce SSEs

ana: short-term workaround for users: include an incremental `seq` inside event JSON and dedupe at app layer. Longer term SDK-level dedupe will cut onboarding friction.

mike: once PRs land add an E2E that simulates abort+reconnect and asserts no duplicate payloads delivered to user callbacks. Also add a debug trace when dedupe skips an event.

ana: PR coming with a small nginx repro and a curl script. I'll paste links here when ready. :thumbsup:
